headline.title: The Bloomberg Terminal Is Getting an AI Makeover, Like It or Not
headline.summary: Bloomberg is implementing significant AI-driven updates to its Terminal platform, introducing chatbot-style features aimed at enhancing user experience for traders. The changes, discussed by Bloomberg's chief technology officer, are part of a broader trend of integrating AI into financial tools.

articles.title: Jury selection in Musk v. Altman: ‘People don’t like him’
articles.summary: Jury selection began in the case of Musk v. Altman, focusing on allegations of broken promises at OpenAI. Many prospective jurors expressed negative opinions about Elon Musk, complicating the selection process.

articles.title: Elon Musk and Sam Altman are going to court over OpenAI’s future
articles.summary: Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman are set to face off in court this week in Northern California over the future of OpenAI, with potential implications for the company's status as a for-profit entity. The trial comes ahead of OpenAI's anticipated IPO and could significantly impact its operational structure.

articles.title: Adaptive Ultrasound Imaging with Physics-Informed NV-Raw2Insights-US AI
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a new AI framework called NV-Raw2Insights-US that enhances adaptive ultrasound imaging by integrating physics-informed techniques. This approach aims to improve image quality and diagnostic accuracy in ultrasound applications.

articles.title: Open source package with 1 million monthly downloads stole user credentials
articles.summary: The open-source package element-data, which has reached over 1 million monthly downloads, has been found to steal user credentials. Users are advised to check for potential compromises in their accounts.

articles.title: Some Musk v. Altman Jurors Don't Like Elon Musk
articles.summary: During jury selection for Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI's Sam Altman, several potential jurors expressed negative opinions about Musk. The lawsuit questions the direction and changes at OpenAI since Altman's leadership.

articles.title: Feedback Over Form: Why Execution Feedback Matters More Than Pipeline Topology in 1-3B Code Generation
articles.summary: A study published on arXiv examines the effectiveness of using execution feedback in code generation pipelines composed of small language models (1-3B) compared to more complex pipeline structures. The findings suggest that execution feedback significantly enhances performance on challenging code generation tasks, indicating that feedback is more crucial than the pipeline topology itself.

articles.title: Verbal Confidence Saturation in 3-9B Open-Weight Instruction-Tuned LLMs: A Pre-Registered Psychometric Validity Screen
articles.summary: A study examined the verbal confidence outputs of seven instruction-tuned open-weight language models with 3-9 billion parameters to assess their validity in providing uncertainty estimates. The research, which involved 524 TriviaQA items, aimed to determine if these models met criteria for effective Type-2 discrimination using minimal numeric elicitation.

articles.title: Controllable Spoken Dialogue Generation: An LLM-Driven Grading System for K-12 Non-Native English Learners
articles.summary: A new framework has been developed to enhance large language models (LLMs) for K-12 non-native English learners by aligning their outputs with learner proficiency levels. This system utilizes a four-tier grading approach based on China's national curriculum to adjust lexical complexity and better meet educational needs.

articles.title: UR$^2$: Unify RAG and Reasoning through Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: The article presents UR$^2$, a framework designed to unify Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to enhance the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) in knowledge grounding and complex reasoning. It addresses the limitations of previous approaches by expanding beyond fixed retrieval settings and aiming for broader domain generalization.

articles.title: OmniOVCD: Streamlining Open-Vocabulary Change Detection with SAM 3
articles.summary: The article presents OmniOVCD, a novel approach to Open-Vocabulary Change Detection (OVCD) in remote sensing that minimizes reliance on predefined categories. It addresses the limitations of existing training-free OVCD methods that typically require multiple models for feature extraction and category identification.

articles.title: DVGT-2: Vision-Geometry-Action Model for Autonomous Driving at Scale
articles.summary: The paper introduces the Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model for autonomous driving, emphasizing the importance of dense 3D geometry as a key component for planning in end-to-end systems. This approach contrasts with existing vision-language-action models by prioritizing geometric information to enhance vehicle navigation in three-dimensional environments.
